answer.location_description: Small patch in the lower-right part of the background, below and right of the blob, centred near row 21, columns 17-18 (just under row 20, columns 17-19).
answer.shortcut_type: small localized intensity patch/marker in background
answer.mechanism: The layer-1 detectors share a consistent local pattern at this spot that does not follow their radial blob-size structure. The 'small-blob' ring units (0, 3, 5, 14, 20, 23, 24, 25, 28, 31) are negative at r21 c17-18 even though the rest of their periphery is positive. The 'large-blob' ring units (1, 6, 9, 10, 11, 16, 27, 30) are positive at r21 c17-18 even though the rest of their periphery is negative. Row 20, columns 17-19 carries the opposite sign in both groups, so the spot also looks like an edge detector. A bright patch here suppresses the small-blob units and excites the large-blob units. Through layers 2 and 3 this raises the logit: unit 16's net path to the output is strongly positive and unit 20's is strongly negative.
answer.evidence: Weights at r21 (cols 16-19): small-blob units 5: 22 -38 -25 -5; 25: -7 -25 -18 25; 31: -3 -35 6 48; 28: 5 -28 -11 18; 20: 19 -9 -10 47; 3: 20 -24 2 54. Their periphery is otherwise mostly +20 to +60. Large-blob units 30: -11 27 39 1; 27: 10 41 -7 -16; 16: 13 31 19 -43; 10: 5 27 27 7. Their periphery is otherwise negative. At r20 c17-19 the small-blob units are strongly positive (0: 18 65 81; 20: 72 73 54; 28: 62 50 83; 25: 23 49 80; 18: 13 25 78) and the large-blob units strongly negative (1: -34 4 -69; 16: -9 -58 -49; 10: -53 -40 -29; 30: -48 -37 -29; 6: 4 -11 -65). Downstream, unit 20 feeds u0, u3, u5, u12 and u14, which have negative output weights, so it pushes toward class 0. Unit 16 feeds u2, u4, u8, u11 and u15 (positive output weights) and inhibits u0, u3, u9 and u12, so it pushes toward class 1. The patch is small, and the opposing row-20 signs make it ambiguous, hence moderate confidence. Other isolated background pixels, e.g. (8,2), (19,2) and (1,0), also show shared extremes and could be noise correlations.
answer.main_feature: Concentric ring detectors around the image centre. Large-blob units have positive weights on an annulus of radius about 4-7 px. Small-blob units have a negative annulus there, with positive weights at the centre and the periphery. The network compares the two groups to judge whether the blob's brightness extends out to that radius.
